title: The Lazy Struct (A Struct with No Behavior)
pattern: A struct that acts solely as a dumb data container with no behavioral methods, no invariants, and is only accessed by other classes.
why_bad: Indicates that behavior has been stripped from the data, leading to feature envy. The struct doesn't pay for itself as a class/type.
detection: A struct containing only public fields or basic accessors, with no domain logic methods of its own.
counterexample: Simple data structures (DTOs) used strictly for serialization or boundary transport between separate subsystems.
fix: Move associated behaviors into this struct, or inline/merge it into the primary consuming class.
source: Fowler, *Refactoring*, Chapter 3 ("Bad Smells - Data Class / Lazy Class"); Joshua Kerievsky, *Refactoring to Patterns* (2004).
